A set of twelve biographies of Julius Caesar and the first eleven emperors, from Augustus to Domitian, written in Latin by Suetonius around 121. He was then a secretary to the emperor Hadrian, with access to the imperial archives, and quotes letters of Augustus that survive nowhere else.

Suetonius does not tell a story year by year, as Tacitus does. He sorts each life by topic: family, career, looks, habits, vices, omens and death. That leaves room for gossip and scandal, and much of what people remember about Nero or Caligula comes from here.

The book became the model for biography in the Middle Ages. Einhard used it for his life of Charlemagne, and it has been read, copied and filmed ever since.
